plan.goal: Build a playable browser Minecraft-style MVP (React 18 + three.js + Vite) with a pure, deterministic, Node-testable engine in src/engine/ that matches the spec exactly. Add a three.js renderer and a React UI on top: menu, infinite seeded chunks, mining and building, inventory, crafting, day/night cycle, HUD, debug overlay and localStorage saves. All textures are generated in code.

steps.step: Implement blocks.js exactly per the spec table: fixed id constants, the item ids STICK=100 to COAL=103, getBlock/getItem with RangeError on unknown ids, Infinity hardness for water and bedrock, tool/drop/maxStack/placeable, isSolid and isTransparent. Also create src/engine/tiles.js, a pure atlas layout: ATLAS_TILES_PER_ROW, a tile index per block face (grass top/side/bottom, log top/side, others uniform), a tile per non-block item for icons, and a crack-stage tile range, plus a helper tileUV(tileIndex) that returns [u0,v0,u1,v1] in [0,1].

Implement noise.js: hashSeed (string/number → uint32 with a good string hash so 'abc'≠'abd'), createRng (e.g. mulberry32), and createNoise2D (seeded gradient/simplex noise clamped to [-1,1] and continuous). Implement daynight.js: DAY_LENGTH=1200, and skyState with t correct mod 1 for negative input, sunAngle=2πt, a continuous daylight in [0.15,1] that is exactly 1 at t=0.25 and 0.15 at t=0.75 (e.g. a cosine mapping), and isNight for t in (0.5,1).

Implement world.js. Write chunkIndex. generateChunk must produce: a height from world-coordinate noise clamped to [12,40]; bedrock at y=0; grass/sand top, 3 dirt/sand below it, stone down to y=1; water to SEA_LEVEL; ores from a per-chunk seeded RNG (coal only at y≤40 with at least one guaranteed, iron only at y≤24); trees only on grass with local trunk x/z in 2..13, a 4–6 log trunk and leaves only in AIR cells inside the chunk. createWorld must cache chunks lazily and support flat mode (bedrock only). Write getBlockAt/setBlockAt with floor-division coordinates for negatives, out-of-range y behavior and RangeError, and an edits map that drops an edit when a block is reverted to its generated value. Also write getSurfaceHeight, and serializeWorld/deserializeWorld with sorted edits, version check and round-trip identity. Expose a chunk version/dirty counter so the renderer can detect edits.

Implement inventory.js (all pure: createInventory, addItem that fills existing stacks first and then empty slots and respects maxStack, removeFromSlot, selectSlot with RangeError, scrollSelection with wrap-around, moveStack for move/merge/swap, selectedItem), crafting.js (craft for 2x2/3x3 grids by id with shifted shaped recipes, the 3x3-only pickaxes, the shapeless planks and glass, extra items invalidating the recipe; pure consumeIngredients) and mining.js (canHarvest, breakTime formula with tool speeds and Infinity for water/bedrock, dropsFor).

Create the procedural texture atlas in src/render/textures.js. Draw one 16x16 pixel-art tile per tiles.js entry on a canvas (grass top/side/bottom, log rings vs bark, ores, glass with transparent center, leaves with alpha holes, translucent water, items such as stick, pickaxes and coal), plus 10 crack stages. Export a THREE.CanvasTexture with NearestFilter and no mipmaps, an iconDataURL(id) for UI icons, and a crack texture/material factory. The code must be deterministic, using createRng.

Implement mesher.js buildChunkMesh(world, cx, cz). For each non-air block emit faces where the neighbor is AIR, or transparent with a different id. Read neighbors across chunks through getBlockAt, with bedrock below 0 and air above 63. Emit world-space quads with outward normals, CCW indices seen from outside, and UVs from tiles.js. Split output into opaque and transparent (water, glass, leaves) typed arrays. Read the chunk array directly for in-chunk neighbors, for speed.

Implement raycast.js: an Amanatides–Woo DDA with an unnormalized direction, AIR/WATER skipped, the origin-inside-a-solid case returning face [0,0,0] and distance 0, and the hit face normal plus the euclidean entry distance, or null beyond maxDistance. Implement physics.js: constants, createPlayer, pure stepPlayer (yaw-based direction, normalized diagonals, walk/sprint/sneak speeds without inertia, gravity capped at terminal velocity, ≤0.05 s substeps, axis-wise Y→X→Z AABB collision that snaps feet to the block top, onGround and ceiling handling, a jump that clears exactly 1 block, sneak edge guard, water modifiers, flying mode), collidesAt and canPlaceBlock.

Build presentational React UI components driven only by props/callbacks (no three.js). They are: MainMenu (title, random seed field, New World, Continue shown only when a save exists, render-distance slider 2–8 with default 4), HUD (crosshair, hotbar with atlas icons and counts, item name toast for 2 s, underwater tint), InventoryScreen (36 slots, click to pick up and drop stacks via moveStack, 2x2 crafting and an optional 3x3 table mode using craft/consumeIngredients, plus an output slot), PauseMenu (Continue/Save/Quit to menu) and DebugOverlay (FPS, XYZ, chunk, facing, targeted block, seed, time). Add src/game/save.js (localStorage key 'mc-mvp-save': save/load/hasSave of the world string, player position/yaw/pitch, inventory and time) and the CSS.

Build the three.js game runtime as a plain class with no React. src/render/ChunkManager.js loads and unloads chunk meshes around the player within the render distance and builds at most ~2 meshes per frame, nearest first, rebuilding the edited chunk and its border neighbors; opaque uses a Lambert material, water is translucent, glass and leaves use alphaTest. src/render/Sky.js handles sky color, sun/moon sprites, ambient and directional light following daylight, and fog at the render distance. src/game/input.js handles pointer lock, mouse look with pitch clamped to ±89°, WASD/space/shift/ctrl, double-tap W sprint, F to fly, 1–9 and the wheel, and mouse buttons. src/game/Game.js runs the loop: stepPlayer, the camera at EYE_HEIGHT, a 5-block raycast with a wireframe outline, hold-to-mine with breakTime and crack overlay progress that resets on target change, drops going to the inventory, right-click placement with a canPlaceBlock check that consumes 1 item, right-click on a crafting table opening the 3x3 grid, middle-click pick block, the day clock, spawning at getSurfaceHeight+1, and a 30 s autosave via save.js. It exposes state snapshots/events for the UI (inventory, selected slot, debug info, underwater, open screens) and methods to pause, resume, save and dispose.

Wire everything into the entry point. App.jsx switches between menu and game, creates a Game on a canvas container (new world from the seed or Continue from save.js), subscribes the UI components to game state, and routes the keys: E for the inventory (releasing pointer lock), Esc for pause plus a save-on-pause, F3 for debug. It applies inventory edits made in the UI back to the game and disposes it cleanly on Quit. main.jsx renders App and imports styles. Verify that npm test and npm run build pass and that npm run dev plays end to end with no console errors.

doneWhen: npm test passes, including the hidden edge-case tests for every engine function contract
npm run build completes without errors
Nothing in src/engine imports three, react or the DOM, and the engine runs under node --test; pure functions never mutate their arguments
npm run dev shows the main menu with seed, New World/Continue and the render-distance slider, and starts a playable world where chunks stream in and out without stutter
Mining with crack progress, placement, inventory with 2x2 crafting, 3x3 crafting at a crafting table, hotbar, flying, water, day/night sky, F3 debug overlay and pause all work
Autosave every 30 s and on pause to localStorage 'mc-mvp-save', and Continue restores the world edits, player position/look, inventory and time of day
No console errors, and ~60 fps at render distance 4
risks: Exact edge cases in the contracts (physics snapping feet to integer y and the 1-vs-2-block jump, the raycast origin inside a solid, serialize ordering and round-trip, negative-coordinate chunk math, edit removal on revert) are covered by hidden tests and are easy to get subtly wrong

Tree and ore generation has to be deterministic per chunk and keep leaves inside the chunk while the height stays seamless across chunks; generation and meshing that are too slow will drop the frame rate
Cross-wave contract drift: tiles.js atlas layout shared by mesher.js and textures.js, and the Game.js state/event API consumed by the UI components and App.jsx, must be agreed exactly
Transparency sorting and depth problems between water, glass and leaves; three.js geometry/material disposal leaks when chunks unload or the user quits to the menu
Pointer lock interacting with the React overlays (E/Esc/F3 handling, the browser consuming Esc, Ctrl+W closing the tab) can produce stuck input or console errors

notes: Before wave 4, fix the Game.js state/event API in writing (snapshot shape, subscribe/emit, and methods such as setInventory, openScreen, pause/resume/save/dispose). The UI components in wave 4 are built before Game.js in wave 5, so they need this contract to code against.

Pause must be driven by `pointerlockchange` (lock lost with no inventory/crafting screen open means pause plus save), not by an Esc keydown: the browser consumes Esc while the pointer is locked. Gameplay input must be ignored whenever a screen is open or the lock is lost, and mining progress reset.

Define who owns the crafting grid and the cursor-held stack. When the inventory or crafting-table screen closes, return those items to the inventory via addItem so they are not lost, and keep them out of the save. Taking the craft output must call consumeIngredients and recompute craft.

World: setBlockAt must update both the cached chunk array and the edits map, because the mesher reads chunk arrays directly. serializeWorld must emit exactly the keys version, seed, flat, edits in that order; the chunk version/dirty counter must stay out of the JSON. deserializeWorld must drop edits equal to the generated value so the round trip is string-identical.

main.jsx currently defines an inline placeholder App; replace it with an import of src/App.jsx and the CSS. Call preventDefault on F3, on the wheel, on middle and right click (contextmenu), and on Ctrl-combined movement keys where possible, to avoid browser side effects.

sessions.summary: Implemented noise.js (hashSeed, createRng, createNoise2D) and daynight.js (DAY_LENGTH, skyState). The visible noise and day/night tests pass; the other failing tests belong to unimplemented modules owned by other steps. npm run build was not run.

Step 1 (wave 1) is done. I wrote two engine files, both pure ESM with no three, react or DOM imports.

**src/engine/blocks.js**
- Exports the block ids 0–14 and the item ids 100–103 as named constants.
- `getBlock(id)` returns `{id, name, solid, transparent, hardness, tool, drop}` as a fresh object. Water and bedrock have hardness `Infinity`.
- `getItem(id)` returns `{id, name, maxStack, placeable}` for blocks and items. Pickaxes have `maxStack` 1. `placeable` is false for AIR and WATER.
- Unknown or non-integer ids throw `RangeError`.
- `isSolid` and `isTransparent` follow the table and throw `RangeError` for unknown ids.

**src/engine/tiles.js**
- Atlas: 16 px tiles, 8 per row, 4 rows, 32 tile slots.
- `TILE` holds named tile indices 0–19. The crack stages are 20–29 (`CRACK_FIRST_TILE`, `CRACK_STAGES`).
- `blockTile(blockId, face='side')` takes `'top' | 'bottom' | 'side'`. Grass bottom uses the dirt tile, and log top and bottom share a tile. Other blocks are uniform.
- `itemTile(id)` returns the tile for an item, or the block's top tile for a block.
- `crackTile(stage)` takes 0–9.
- `tileUV(i)` returns `[u0,v0,u1,v1]` with v growing downward. Textures must therefore use `flipY = false`. Please pass this on to the textures.js and mesher steps.
- Invalid tile indices and crack stages throw `RangeError`.

**Verification**
- `npm test`: the blocks table test passes. The other failures are in stubs that belong to other steps (world, inventory, crafting, mining).
- `npm run build` passes.
- I could not run ad-hoc `node -e` checks because the shell denied them. The RangeError paths and `tileUV` values were verified by reading the code only.

I couldn't run any other command, so the hidden contract cases (seamless heights, tree placement, the guaranteed coal block, an exact save round trip) are checked only by reading the code, not by running it.

**What's in the file**
- Constants and `chunkIndex`.
- `generateChunk(seed, cx, cz)`:
  - Terrain height comes from three noise layers in world coordinates, clamped to [12, 40], so columns match across chunk borders.
  - Columns follow the spec: bedrock at y = 0, grass or sand on top, 3 dirt or sand below, stone down to y = 1, water up to sea level.
  - Coal (y ≤ 40) and iron (y ≤ 24) only replace stone, using a random generator seeded per chunk. A fallback guarantees at least one coal block per chunk.
  - Trees grow only on grass, with the trunk at local x/z 2–13, 4–6 logs tall. Leaves go only into air cells inside the chunk, and trees are kept apart from each other.
- `createWorld(seed, { flat })` generates chunks lazily and caches them. Flat mode is bedrock only.
- `getBlockAt` handles negative coordinates (x = -1 is chunk -1, local 15), returns bedrock below 0 and air from 64 up.
- `setBlockAt` throws `RangeError` for y outside 0–63 or an unknown id. It updates both the cached chunk array and the edits list, and drops the edit when a block is set back to its generated value.
- `getSurfaceHeight` returns -1 if the column has no solid block.
- `serializeWorld` writes exactly the keys version, seed, flat, edits, with edits sorted by x, then y, then z. `deserializeWorld` throws on any version other than 1, and edits equal to the generated value are dropped, so the round trip gives the same string.

**Extra exports for the renderer (wave 5)**
- `getChunk(world, cx, cz)` returns the cached chunk array with edits applied. The mesher can read it directly.
- `hasChunk` and `unloadChunk`. Unloading keeps the edits, and they are applied again when the chunk regenerates.
- `getChunkVersion(world, cx, cz)` and `world.version`. An edit bumps its own chunk and, if it is on a chunk border, the neighbouring chunk. Neither counter goes into the save.
- `terrainHeight(seed, x, z)`.

Implementei `buildChunkMesh` em `src/engine/mesher.js`. As faces seguem o contrato de culling: a face sai quando o vizinho é AIR, ou transparente com id diferente. Fora do chunk, os vizinhos vêm de `getBlockAt`. Abaixo de y=0 conta como BEDROCK e acima de 63 como AIR. As posições estão em coordenadas de mundo, as normais apontam para fora, e os índices são anti-horários vistos de fora. Conferi o sentido de cada face à mão, com produto vetorial. As UVs vêm de `tileUV(blockTile(...))`, com v crescendo para baixo. A saída vai separada em `opaque` e `transparent`.

I finished step 7: `src/engine/raycast.js` and `src/engine/physics.js`. Both of their tests pass ("raycast: acerta o bloco à frente" and "física: cai e para no chão"), and `npm run build` finishes without errors. `npm test` still fails 3 of 11 tests (inventory, crafting, mining) because those modules belong to other sessions and still throw "não implementado". I could only run `npm test` and `npm run build`, so the edge cases below are reasoned through, not run.

**Raycast:**
- Walks the voxels with the Amanatides & Woo DDA. The direction can be unnormalized, and AIR and WATER are not targets.
- If the origin is already inside a block, it returns that block with face [0,0,0] and distance 0.
- A hit returns the outward face normal and the distance from the origin to the entry point. The result is `null` past `maxDistance`, for a zero direction, or once the ray is above the world and still going up.
- Below y=0 the ray hits bedrock, because `getBlockAt` returns BEDROCK for y < 0 (same rule as the mesher).
- It avoids returning -0 in coordinates and distance, so exact-equality checks don't fail on it.

**Physics:**
- `createPlayer`, `collidesAt` and `canPlaceBlock` follow the spec. Faces that only touch don't count as overlapping.
- `stepPlayer` is pure and splits `dt` into steps of at most 0.05 s. Collision sweeps axis by axis (Y, then X, then Z) and checks every cell crossed, so it doesn't pass through blocks even at terminal velocity. Landing puts the feet exactly on the integer block top and sets `onGround`; hitting a ceiling zeroes `velocity[1]`.
- Movement follows the yaw directions in the spec, with normalized diagonals and walk/sprint/sneak speed applied directly (no inertia). By my calculation the jump peaks at about 1.05–1.27 blocks depending on the step size: enough for one block, never two.
- Sneak on the ground searches for the farthest point that still has a block underneath, so the player stops right at the edge.
- In water: gravity is 1/4, falling is capped at 3 blocks/s, and jump rises at 3 blocks/s.
- Flying: no gravity; jump rises and sneak descends at `WALK_SPEED`, and collision still applies.

**Choices the spec leaves open (a hidden test could expect otherwise):**
- On a jump step, gravity is applied in the same step, so `velocity[1]` comes back as 9 minus gravity × the step, not exactly 9.
- While flying, Shift only descends and doesn't slow horizontal movement; horizontal speed is walk or sprint.
- Sneak takes priority over sprint.
- When a horizontal move is blocked, that axis's velocity is set to 0.

Written: `MainMenu.jsx`, `HUD.jsx`, `InventoryScreen.jsx`, `PauseMenu.jsx`, `DebugOverlay.jsx`, `ItemIcon.jsx`, `styles.css` and `src/game/save.js`.

Two imports depend on other sessions' files: `ItemIcon` uses `iconDataURL` from `src/render/textures.js` (wave 2), and `InventoryScreen` uses `craft`/`consumeIngredients` from `crafting.js`. When I looked, `inventory.js` was still a stub, so `InventoryScreen`'s `addItem` call will fail until that step lands.

The props each component expects, which `App.jsx` and `Game.js` need to match:
- **`MainMenu`**: `{ hasSave, onNewWorld(seed, renderDistance), onContinue(renderDistance) }`. The slider runs 2 to 8, default 4, and the seed field starts random.
- **`HUD`**: `{ inventory, underwater }`. It shows the crosshair, the hotbar with icons and counts, a 2 s item-name toast and the underwater tint.
- **`InventoryScreen`**: `{ inventory, mode: 'inventory' | 'table', onInventoryChange(inv), onClose }`.
  - It owns the crafting grid (2x2 or 3x3) and the cursor-held stack.
  - Clicking the output slot calls `consumeIngredients` and recomputes `craft`.
  - On unmount it returns the grid and cursor items to the inventory with `addItem` and calls `onInventoryChange`, so they never reach the save.
  - Left click picks up or drops a stack; right click takes half or places one.
- **`PauseMenu`**: `{ onResume, onSave, onQuit }`.
- **`DebugOverlay`**: `{ info: { fps, position, chunk, facing, target, seed, time } }`.
- **`save.js`**: exports `hasSave`, `save({ world, player, inventory, time })`, `load()`, `clearSave` and `SAVE_KEY = 'mc-mvp-save'`. `world` is the `serializeWorld` string, and `load()` returns null for a missing or corrupt save.

I did not touch `main.jsx`, since the wiring belongs to a later wave.

I wrote step 9's four files, but none of their code has been bundled or run yet. `npm run build` passes, but `main.jsx` is still the placeholder, so it doesn't include any of the new files. `npm test` gives 8 passing and 3 failing. All 3 failures are the unimplemented stubs in inventory.js, crafting.js and mining.js, which belong to step 4, not my step.

Two missing pieces will break or degrade wave 6:
- **`src/render/textures.js` does not exist** (step 5). `Game.js` and the existing `ItemIcon.jsx` both import it, so the wave-6 build fails until it is written. Game.js looks for the atlas texture under a few likely export names; if it finds none, the game runs with plain placeholder colours instead of real textures.
- **Inventory, crafting and mining are stubs that throw.** The hotbar, mining drops, placing blocks and crafting won't work until step 4 is done.

**Files:**
- **`src/render/ChunkManager.js`** loads chunk meshes nearest-first within the render distance. Each frame it builds at most 2 new chunks within about 8 ms, and rebuilds any chunk whose world version changed (the edited chunk and its border neighbours). It drops meshes outside the distance plus 1, and drops cached world chunks outside the distance plus 3. It splits the transparent mesh into water (translucent) and glass/leaves (cut-out). Edits survive unloading because `world.js` keeps them separately.
- **`src/render/Sky.js`** colours the sky from `skyState`, with an orange tint at sunrise and sunset. It has square sun and moon sprites, ambient and directional light that follow `daylight`, and fog ending at the render distance.
- **`src/game/input.js`** handles pointer lock and mouse look (pitch limited to ±89°), WASD, Space, Shift, Ctrl or double-tap W to sprint, F to fly, 1–9 and the wheel for the hotbar, and the three mouse buttons. It blocks the browser defaults for F3, the wheel, middle and right click, and Ctrl+movement keys.
- **`src/game/Game.js`** is the game loop and the API the UI uses.

**Game API for App.jsx (wave 6):**
- **Constructor:** `new Game(container, { seed, renderDistance, saveData, atlas })`. `saveData` is the object from `save.js` `load()` and restores the world, player, inventory and time. `atlas` is an optional texture that overrides the one from textures.js.
- **Snapshot:** `subscribe(fn)` returns an unsubscribe function, and `getSnapshot()` returns a new object on every change, so it works with `useSyncExternalStore`. Shape: `{ screen: null|'inventory'|'table'|'pause', locked, inventory, underwater, showDebug, debug, flying }`. `debug` has the fields `DebugOverlay` expects.
- **Methods:** `setInventory(inv)` (connect it to `InventoryScreen`'s `onInventoryChange`), `openScreen`, `closeScreen`, `pause`, `resume`, `save`, `toggleDebug`, `dispose`.
- **Keys:** Game already handles E, F3 and Esc. App must not bind them again, or the inventory will open and close on the same key press. App should only render from the snapshot and call those methods.
- **Pause:** losing the pointer lock with no screen open pauses and saves. If the browser refuses to re-lock right after an Esc, the game goes back to the pause menu instead of running without a menu.
- **Click-to-play hint:** App should show one when `!locked && screen === null`.
- **Autosave:** every 30 s, postponed while a crafting screen is open. Closing a screen returns the crafting-grid items through `InventoryScreen`'s unmount and `setInventory`.

I wrote `src/App.jsx` and replaced `src/main.jsx`. Neither `npm test` nor `npm run build` passes yet, but every failure comes from files from earlier waves that are missing or still stubs. Because the build can't finish, nothing in the game has been run.

**What I built:**
- **`src/main.jsx`** now imports the real `App` and `ui/styles.css`. I left out StrictMode so development mode doesn't create two WebGL contexts.
- **`src/App.jsx`** switches between the main menu and the game.
  - "Novo mundo" passes the seed (a numeric string becomes a number) and the render distance. "Continuar" loads the save from `save.js` and only shows when a save exists.
  - The game view creates the `Game` in a container and disposes of it when it unmounts. The UI reads game state through `useSyncExternalStore`.
  - It shows the HUD, the F3 debug overlay, and the inventory screen in 2x2 or 3x3 mode. The 2x2 and 3x3 screens are separate instances, so items in the crafting grid go back to the inventory when the screen closes.
  - The pause menu has Continue, Save and Quit; Quit saves, disposes the game and refreshes the menu's "Continuar" button. It also shows a "Clique para jogar" hint when the mouse isn't locked, and an error panel if the game fails to start.
- E, F3, Esc, pause-on-unlock and the `preventDefault` calls were already handled in `Game.js` and `input.js`, as the review asked, so I didn't add them again in App.

**Why the commands fail:**
- **`npm run build`:** `src/render/textures.js` (wave 2) doesn't exist, and both `ItemIcon.jsx` and `Game.js` import it. Those two missing imports are the only build errors.
- **`npm test`:** 3 of 11 fail because `inventory.js`, `crafting.js` and `mining.js` (wave 2) are still stubs that throw "não implementado".

The missing pieces are written and both checks now pass. `npm test` passes all 11 tests, and `npm run build` completes; its only warning is that the bundle is over 500 kB. I did not run `npm run dev`, so the game itself has not been played in a browser. I checked the gameplay wiring by reading the code only.

**What I wrote this session:**
- **`src/engine/inventory.js`**: all the inventory functions from the spec, each returning a new object without changing its input.
- **`src/engine/crafting.js`**: `craft` takes a 2x2 or 3x3 grid and handles all six recipes. Shaped recipes work even when shifted in the grid, the pickaxes need the 3x3 grid, and any extra item cancels the recipe. `consumeIngredients` returns a new grid.
- **`src/engine/mining.js`**: `canHarvest`, `breakTime` (using the spec's formula, with pickaxe speeds 2 and 4, and `Infinity` for water and bedrock) and `dropsFor`.
- **`src/render/textures.js`**: the atlas of 16x16 tiles, drawn in code with a seeded random generator, so it looks the same every time.
  - Grass has different top, side and bottom tiles, and logs have rings on top and bark on the sides.
  - Leaves have see-through holes, and glass is clear in the middle.
  - There are tiles for the ores, items, pickaxes, and 10 crack stages for mining.
  - `createAtlasTexture()` gives a new texture with the nearest-pixel filter. `iconDataURL(id)` gives cached icons: blocks drawn as small 3D cubes, items drawn flat.

**Small fixes to earlier code:**
- **`src/engine/physics.js`**: the player no longer counts as standing on the ground after bumping their head on a ceiling.
- **`src/game/Game.js`**: a saved hotbar slot outside 0–8 now resets to 0 instead of causing an error.
- **`src/ui/ItemIcon.jsx`**: errors from building an icon are now caught, so an unknown item can't crash the screen.

**What I checked by reading:**
- The UI uses the new modules' return values correctly.
- The pause comes from losing the mouse lock, not from the Esc key.
- When the inventory or crafting screen closes, items left in the crafting grid or held on the cursor go back to the inventory.
- Taking a crafted item uses up the ingredients.
- Browser defaults are blocked for F3, the mouse wheel, middle click and right click.
- Saves use the `mc-mvp-save` key, with an autosave every 30 s.
- Right-clicking a crafting table opens the 3x3 grid.

The hidden edge-case tests were not available, so the engine is only checked against the 11 visible tests and by reading it against the spec.
